topics.title: Benchmark III: Students will be able to identify basic human rights.

outcomes.text: Define and distinguish among citizen, global citizen, and digital or cyber citizen.
Define human rights.
Distinguish between rights and responsibilities.
Define tolerance.
Explain why accepting social and cultural differences supports harmonious living.
Explain how attitudes can produce conflict or peace.
Identify causes of disagreements among individuals, peers, households, and neighborhoods.
Resolve conflicts through discussion.
Identify everyday etiquette, including manners, respect, helpfulness, dignified work, and discipline.
Describe civic sense using traffic rules, cleanliness, and WASH examples.
List and describe different forms of communication.
Investigate how communication methods have changed over time.

topics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to explain the concept of nation and nationalism.

subtopics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to explain the concept of nation and nationalism.

outcomes.text: Describe the meanings of nation and nationalism.
Relate to being a proud member of a nation.
Describe culture and its components.
Define diversity.
Recall the diverse cultural groups living in Pakistan.
Illustrate Pakistan’s cultural diversity through examples of religion, crafts, languages, festivals, clothing, foods, music, and art.
Identify major Pakistani social groups and their characteristics, including gender, religion, ethnicity, and ability.
Recognize how minority communities celebrate their festivals.
Explain how diversity helps society prosper.

subtopics.title: Benchmark II: Students will be able to explain the main events and major contributions that led to the formation of Pakistan.

outcomes.text: Discuss how Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Allama Muhammad Iqbal, and Fatima Jinnah helped create Pakistan.

topics.title: Standard 3: All students will identify the purpose of a government and constitution, and describe the components of a democratic government used to make decisions, seek consensus, and resolve conflicts.

outcomes.text: Define and distinguish between a state and a government.
Explain what a constitution is.
Define general elections.
Show how voting works and how it leads to government formation.
Describe what a leader is.
Discuss the qualities that make someone a good leader.

topics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to trace the advent of civilizations, their timelines, and the chronology of major historical events.

outcomes.text: Define history and explain why studying it is important.
Place Mesopotamian, Egyptian, and Indus Valley civilizations on a timeline.
Describe everyday life, society, and culture in the Indus Valley Civilization.

topics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to find and locate places on a map using BOLTSS, scale, longitudes, and latitudes.

outcomes.text: Describe what maps and globes are.
List the uses of maps and globes.
Identify the main elements of a map or globe.
Locate all continents and major oceans and seas.
Recognize cardinal directions and use a compass to identify them.
Describe and label a map’s borders, orientation, legend, title, scale, and source.

topics.title: Benchmark II: Students will be able to identify various landforms and their distinctive features.

subtopics.title: Benchmark II: Students will be able to identify various landforms and their distinctive features.

outcomes.text: Identify major landforms and their types in Pakistan.

topics.title: Benchmark III: Students will be able to explain how the physical environment affects the lifestyle of people.

subtopics.title: Benchmark III: Students will be able to explain how the physical environment affects the lifestyle of people.

outcomes.text: Define and distinguish weather from climate.
Explain how Pakistan’s physical environment affects people’s lifestyles.

topics.title: Benchmark IV: Students will be able to determine how people affect the physical environment.

subtopics.title: Benchmark IV: Students will be able to determine how people affect the physical environment.

outcomes.text: Explain positive and negative effects of human activities on nature, including deforestation, dams, and industry.
Identify the importance and interconnectedness of water, sanitation, and hygiene.

topics.title: Benchmark VI: Students will be able to explain the effects of the imbalance of population and resources.

outcomes.text: Explain why a census is important.
Survey regional population distribution and map the region or province.
List major problems caused by overpopulation.
Define growth rate and population density.
Describe factors contributing to population growth in Pakistan.
Determine how population growth affects daily life quality in the community.

topics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to explain how people and societies make economic decisions.

outcomes.text: Recall the concept of scarcity.
Recognize that choices depend on personal needs and available resources.
Define goods and services and give examples.
Identify the functions of consumers and producers.
Distinguish between producers and consumers.
Define types of entrepreneurship and give Pakistani business examples.
Read about at least one Pakistani male and one female entrepreneur.
Describe money’s role and importance in people’s lives.
Apply personal money-management skills involving pocket money, spending, and saving.
Describe banking.
State services provided by banks.

topics.title: Benchmark III: Students will be able to identify basic human rights.

outcomes.text: Establish that everyone has equal rights regardless of religion or ethnicity.
Value and respect differences in people’s opinions.
Explain why free speech matters and use it responsibly.
Recognize ethical behavior for digital citizens and manage online opinion differences.
Suggest ways to promote peace and harmony.
Demonstrate how discussion and negotiation can resolve conflicts at home and school.
Reflect on personal and societal etiquette in the modern world.
Describe mass media and social media.
Investigate the advantages and disadvantages of different communication methods.

topics.title: Standard 3: All students will identify the purpose of a government and constitution, and describe the components of a democratic government used to make decisions, seek consensus, and resolve conflicts.

outcomes.text: Explain why a federal government is necessary.
Explain and assess why a constitution is needed and important.
Explain how federal, provincial, and local governments depend on one another in Pakistan.
Describe the legislature, executive, and judiciary as parts of government.
Explain democracy and why it matters to people.

topics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to trace the advent of civilizations, their timelines, and the chronology of major historical events.

subtopics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to trace the advent of civilizations, their timelines, and the chronology of major historical events.

outcomes.text: Place Mesopotamian, Egyptian, Indus Valley, and Gandhara civilizations on a timeline.
Describe important features of everyday life, society, and culture in ancient Egypt.

topics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to explain the concept of nation and nationalism.

subtopics.title: Benchmark II: Students will be able to explain the main events and major contributions that led to the formation of Pakistan.

outcomes.text: Analyze the contributions of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, Begum Rana Liaquat Ali Khan, Begum Jahanara Shahnawaz, and Chaudhry Rehmat Ali.

topics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to find and locate places on a map using BOLTSS, scale, longitudes, and latitudes.

outcomes.text: Recognize road, tourist, weather, political, and topographical maps.
Recognize the features of latitudes, longitudes, and time zones.
Use latitude and longitude grid references to determine locations.
Apply BOLTSS when using a political or physical map.
Define map scale and its types using diagrams.

topics.title: Benchmark II: Students will be able to identify various landforms and their distinctive features.

subtopics.title: Benchmark II: Students will be able to identify various landforms and their distinctive features.

outcomes.text: Briefly describe the distinctive features of Pakistan’s physical regions.

topics.title: Benchmark III: Students will be able to explain how the physical environment affects the lifestyle of people.

outcomes.text: Describe factors that determine or influence climate.
Explain global warming.
Analyze global warming’s effects on climate change.
Explain how the physical environment influences people’s lifestyles.
Identify occupations such as agriculture, mining, and industry.
Reflect on which occupation they find most appealing.

topics.title: Benchmark VI: Students will be able to explain the effects of the imbalance of population and resources.

outcomes.text: Examine how floods, earthquakes, cyclones, and avalanches occur and affect human life.
Describe food security and assess its necessity in Pakistan.
Suggest safety actions before, during, and after floods or earthquakes.

topics.title: Benchmark I: Students will be able to explain how people and societies make economic decisions.

outcomes.text: Recall the meanings of goods and services.
Distinguish between public and private goods and services.
Define trade, business, and electronic commerce.
Define exports and imports.
State Pakistan’s major imports and exports.
Describe international trade’s importance to Pakistan’s development.
Identify major transportation methods used in trade and business.
Illustrate entrepreneurial skills and competencies with examples.
Discuss the contributions of at least two Pakistani entrepreneurs, including a woman and a man.
Create and present a hypothetical business or enterprise.
Define inflation and evaluate its effect on purchasing power.
List causes and types of inflation.
Explain with examples how barter and trade evolved into using money.
Explain how commercial banks serve individuals and businesses.
Identify the role of Pakistan’s central bank.
